circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, that has served as the venue for the Formula One season finale since 2009. It stands as the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Australian Grand Prix alongside various support categories and earning FIA Grade 1 status. The layout serves as a premier venue for Formula One racing in Australia and features several supporting racing events.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and staged the Austrian Grand Prix for 18 consecutive seasons between 1970 and 1987. Following restructuring and renaming as the A1-Ring, it returned to hosting the Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track positioned along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan's capital, spanning 6. 003 km and ranking among the longest venues in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before being officially designated as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix venue from 2017 onward under the management of Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other international motorsport events. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various racing series and configurations, having previously featured Australian V8 Supercars and hosting 24-hour endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple aspects of racing performance. The facility holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7. 004 km Belgian circuit in Francorchamps has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950, with the Belgian Grand Prix becoming an annual fixture from 1985 onwards, save for two cancelled editions. Known for its challenging layout, this venue has established itself as a cornerstone of the modern championship calendar.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: The Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km racing track located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, hosting the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport series, including world sportscar competitions, American open-wheel racing, and stock car events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading hosted China's Formula One Grand Prix from 2004 until 2019, before resuming in 2024. Located in Shanghai, the facility has expanded its motorsport calendar to include additional racing events alongside its flagship grand prix.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated near villages in Northamptonshire that has served as the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. The track gained historic significance by hosting the inaugural Formula One World Championship race in 1950, and after alternating with other circuits during the 1950s through 1980s, it became the permanent British Grand Prix location from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km permanent circuit near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held within Eastern Europe when it debuted in 1986. Built remarkably quickly over just eight months starting in late 1985, the track was constructed outside the city as a compromise after plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale di Monza, situated near Milan in northern Italy, is a 5. 793 km track established in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. It has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, interrupted only by a 1980 closure for renovation, making it one of Formula One's most enduring venues since the championship's beginning.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland. The circuit hosts major Formula One and Super Formula racing events and accommodates up to 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard corridor. The layout passes by iconic destinations including major casino resorts and entertainment venues, creating a unique urban racing configuration through one of the world's most recognizable hospitality districts.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honours two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in separate racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The circuit returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, with the event now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring 3. 363 miles of track with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by specialist firm Apex Circuit Design, it became the venue for the Miami Grand Prix when it joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbour area. The track is frequently known by the name "Monte Carlo," reflecting its primary location within that particular neighbourhood of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026. The venue earns its "Roller coaster in the Dunes" nickname through steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz combined with dramatic elevation changes that wind through the seaside landscape.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometer motorsport venue featuring a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit that opened in 1940. The track was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident eight years earlier, and now serves as his burial site.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The track also began hosting a Formula E event starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue located around Singapore's Marina Bay, spanning through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design featuring extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple aspects of driver skill and vehicle setup. The venue, which holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators, has established itself as a comprehensive technical challenge in motorsport.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas near Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue hosts premier international motorsport events including MotoGP and the World Endurance Championship, alongside various other racing series including NASCAR and IndyCar events.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently represents Thailand in Formula One while driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and the Le Mans 24 Hours twice with Toyota, making him the sole driver to claim both a Formula One world title and a World Sportscar Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli has secured the 2026 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes, setting the record as the sport's youngest-ever champion. Since his entry to the series in 2025, he has achieved nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One, competing for the Audi team in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish Formula One driver, currently races for Cadillac and has achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes. Over his 13-season career, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One for Alpine, representing his country in the sport's top racing category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One and made seven Grand Prix appearances during the 2024-2025 season. Currently, he competes in the LMP2 category of the Asian Le Mans Series with AF Corse, having previously raced in the European Le Mans Series.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver previously secured a victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian driver competing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, racing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British racing driver Lewis Hamilton competes for Ferrari in Formula One, holding the joint-record of seven World Drivers' Championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Hülkenberg, a German driver, currently races for Audi in Formula One and has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, including a Le Mans 24-hour victory with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 World Championship and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories during his nine-season Formula One career.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen transitioned to endurance racing, currently representing BMW in the World Endurance Championship with the WRT team. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, competing in the sport from 2014 through 2020 before returning for the 2022 and 2023 seasons.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver competing for McLaren who secured the 2025 drivers' championship title with the team. Over his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 14 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver who recently raced for Haas. The highlight of his career came in 2021 when he secured victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing with him extensive experience across 15 seasons and six Grand Prix victories. He achieved his best championship result in 2023 when he finished as runner-up in the drivers' standings while competing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, claiming eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz Jr. is a Spanish Formula One driver currently racing for Williams. The veteran competitor has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12 seasons in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Hunter Sargeant, an American driver, competed in Formula One during the 2023-2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He now races in the FIA World Endurance Championship for Ford, following earlier stints in the LMGT3 category with Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One. He is known by his first name in the sport and has established himself as a competitor on the grid.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen represents the Netherlands in Formula One while competing for Red Bull Racing. He has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024, accumulating 74 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor, drove in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He holds the distinction of being the only driver from his nation to have raced in the sport's top category.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team adopted the Alpine Racing identity beginning in 2021, maintaining its role as Renault's factory operation while promoting the Alpine sports car marque. Previously operating as Renault F1 Team under Groupe Renault ownership, the squad remained affiliated with the manufacturer through the 2025 season before Renault's withdrawal from the championship.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has been involved in Formula One racing through multiple team structures, with the current iteration operating under AMR GP Limited and competing as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-standing and most accomplished team, participating in every world championship since 1950. The squad, famously nicknamed after its emblematic horse symbol, represents an unparalleled continuity and success record in the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American Formula One team in 2014, with operations beginning in the 2016 season. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Swiss engineering firm Sauber Motorsport, established by Peter Sauber in 1970, transitioned from sports car manufacturing to become an independent Formula One constructor starting in 1993, achieving notable success including the 1989 Le Mans 24-hour victory before departing the championship as motorsport's fourth-most experienced active team. The organization and its operational framework were purchased by Audi in 2024 to establish the foundation for Audi's factory entry into Formula One.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company. The team competes under sponsorship arrangements in the sport's premier championship.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has participated in Formula One as both a constructor and power unit supplier since 1954, with the current Brackley-based team operating under a German licence. Following a 2022 restructuring, ownership is divided equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing operations are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as Red Bull's second constructor within the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team within the Red Bull organization's two-team structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from an English base, has been a dominant Formula One outfit since its 2005 establishment by Red Bull GmbH. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its first two decades until Laurent Mekies assumed the principal role in 2025, with Red Bull GmbH also operating the separate Racing Bulls team in the championship.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding an earlier unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the championship and will race under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name in 2026.
